chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the alms-tax (zakat), is it given to one who does not know (the recipients)? He said, 'No, and (not) the alms-tax of fitrah.'
ai.seo_question: Can zakat be given to someone who does not know the eligible recipients?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that ignorance of the specific categories of zakat recipients does not exempt one from the obligation, ruling that such individuals are not eligible to receive it. This ruling is extended to zakat al-fitr, emphasizing that the recipient must possess sufficient knowledge to understand the religious nature of the gift, a principle rooted in the Quranic requirement for recipients to be 'those whose hearts are to be reconciled' (9:60).
